record.category: premium link generator (credit-based, host list only)

free_tier.stated: No free tier is published. The landing page is a host table and nothing else: no price, no allowance, no signup link, no FAQ, no terms. The only other page is an OpenSearch XML descriptor.
free_tier.notes: What the page does state: a host list (alfafile, turbobit, filer.net, 1fichier, ddownload, rapidgator, filestore.to, mega.nz) with asterisks marking 'limited traffic' and 'no guarantee', plus torrent and usenet rows.

per_object_cap.stated: unstated on the page; the asterisks mark hosts where traffic is limited

egress.terms: Not published. A credit balance is implied by the service type but no price or allowance appears on any page reached.

record.interface_detail: The OpenSearch descriptor publishes a GET endpoint: 'https://premium.to/getfile.php?link={searchTerms}'. That is a browser search shortcut, but it is also a public HTTP entry point that takes a link, which a wrapper can call.
record.tooling: The site links to JDownloader, so a JD plugin or manual paste is the intended client. No API documentation exists.
record.chaining: A credit service would slot in exactly where a debrid account does, but without a published price the cost per TB cannot be computed, so it cannot be ranked against the debrid services.

limits.value: unstated; credits are implied, not documented

record.limits_note: The asterisks are the only limit information on the site: 'limited traffic' on alfafile and turbobit, 'no guarantee' on ddownload and rapidgator. Neither is quantified.
record.binding_note: If the service sells credits, the credit balance is what fails first at 1 TiB/month; because no rate is published, only the kind can be named, not the point of failure.

identity_cost.detail: No signup page is linked from the landing page, so the registration fields are unverified. A paid credit service of this shape normally requires an email account; that is inference, not observation.

record.reliability_note: The public endpoint returned HTTP 200 with a zero-byte body when handed a non-host URL, which is the classic false 200: a wrapper must check bytes, not status. The site publishes no status page and no terms.
record.confidence_note: The host list, the absence of pricing and the endpoint are all observed; the paid-only verdict is inferred from the absence of any free path. One probe of the endpoint produced a measured empty 200.

evidence.proved: the host table with 'limited traffic' and 'no guarantee' asterisks, torrent and usenet rows, and the total absence of price, allowance or signup text (65 words on the page)
OpenSearch template GET https://premium.to/getfile.php?link={searchTerms}, i.e. the public link-taking endpoint
HTTP 200 with 0 bytes and sha256 e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855; the probe flags it as a false 200 of kind 'empty'
landing page answers: HTTP 200, 4385 bytes, sha256 796b1480e67fb78a...

record.notes: A name that recurs in old debrid lists, still resolving, with almost no published information. The endpoint existing does not make it usable: the empty 200 means a caller learns nothing without a valid host link, and the host list is the only evidence the service does anything.
